sections.markdown:
## C — Stopping regulations, railroad crossings, school buses, emergency vehicles and the Move Over law, police stops, headlights, parking limits, cell phones and littering
Knowledge domain: when a New Jersey driver must stop or slow — signals, railroad crossings, school buses, ice cream trucks, emergency vehicles and the Move Over law — how to handle a police stop, when headlights and high beams are required or forbidden, the exact no-parking distances, and the handheld phone ban with its fines.

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
Most crashes at traffic signals happen in the first few seconds after the light changes, so take care when moving off on a fresh green. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
When a yellow light follows a green, stop before the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely, and if the light changes while you are already in the intersection, continue through with caution. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
A stale green is a light that has already been green for some time, so be ready for it to turn yellow and then red. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A02
A driver must stop at a stop sign and at a red light, whether the red is steady or flashing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A02
A driver must stop when a school bus is picking up or dropping off children or has its red lights flashing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A02
A driver must stop for a blind pedestrian using a white or metallic cane or a trained guide dog, and for a guide dog instructor who is training a dog. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A03
Stop at least 15 feet from a railroad crossing when there are flashing red lights, ringing bells, lowering or lowered gates, or flag signals. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A03
Do not cross the tracks until the gates are up, the bells have stopped ringing and the red lights have stopped flashing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A03
Most trains moving at 60 mph or more need over a mile to stop, so never race a train. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A03
School buses, buses and vehicles carrying hazardous materials must always stop at railroad crossings, so be ready to stop behind them even when no train is signaled. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A03
Never stop on railroad tracks; make sure there is room to get fully across, and if the warning devices start while you are on the tracks, keep going to the other side. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A04
For a school bus with flashing red lights, stop at least 25 feet away on a two-lane road, on a multi-lane highway whose lanes are separated only by lines, or on a privately maintained road. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A04
On a dual-lane highway where you are on the other side of a safety island or raised median from a stopped school bus, slow to 10 mph. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A04
After stopping for a school bus, move on only once its signals are off, and even then watch for children and people with developmental disabilities. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A04
When a school bus has stopped directly in front of a school to load or unload, you may pass it from either direction at no more than 10 mph. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A05
For an ice cream or frozen dessert truck showing flashing red lights and a stop signal arm, yield to anyone crossing to or from it, stop, and then pass at no more than 15 mph. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A05
When an emergency vehicle uses its siren or flashing red or blue lights, steer to the far right, stop and let it pass, then stay at least 300 feet behind any signaling emergency vehicle. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A05
Never park within 200 feet of a fire department vehicle in service, and never drive over a fire hose unless a fire, rescue or police official tells you to. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A05
The Move Over law requires moving into a lane not next to a stopped emergency, tow, highway maintenance or other service vehicle showing flashing lights, or a stopped vehicle using hazard lights, flares or reflective triangles, when safety and traffic allow. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A05
If moving over is impossible, illegal or unsafe, slow to a reasonable speed below the posted limit and be ready to stop. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A05
A Move Over violation carries a fine of $100 to $500, and three or more convictions can also bring motor vehicle points. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A06
When emergency lights appear behind you, signal, slow down and move promptly to the right shoulder or another safe place. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A06
During a police stop, put the vehicle in park, stay inside unless told otherwise, roll down the window, switch on the interior light at night and keep your hands visible, ideally on the steering wheel. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A06
At a traffic stop, New Jersey drivers must show a valid driver license, the vehicle registration and proof of insurance. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A08
Headlights are required from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A08
Headlights are also required whenever visibility is 500 feet or less, whenever the windshield wipers are in use, and in fog, mist, smoke or anything else that cuts visibility. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A08
Parking lights or auxiliary lights may not legally take the place of headlights when headlights are required. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A08
Use high beams only in open country with no traffic in sight, and switch them off when another vehicle approaches or when you are following one. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A08
Recovering from the glare of oncoming high beams can take 3 to 5 seconds, and at 50 mph a driver covers the length of a football field in that blind time. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec07-F30 | anchor: A08
If an oncoming driver has high beams on, look toward the right side of the road until it passes, and never flash your own high beams back. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec07-F31 | anchor: A08
Parking lights are required on vehicles parked anywhere other than business or residential zones. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec07-F32 | anchor: A09
Parking a vehicle more than six inches from the curb is illegal. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec07-F33 | anchor: A10
Do not park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec07-F34 | anchor: A10
Do not park within 25 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, except at alleys. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec07-F35 | anchor: A10
Do not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing or within 50 feet of a stop sign. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec07-F36 | anchor: A10
Do not park within 20 feet of a fire station driveway, or within 75 feet of the entrance on the opposite side of the street. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec07-F37 | anchor: A10
Using a handheld phone or texting device while driving on any public road is a primary offense, while a hands-free phone is legal but strongly discouraged. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec07-F38 | anchor: A11
A handheld phone may be used only in an emergency such as a fire, a traffic crash, a serious road hazard, a medical emergency or a hazardous material emergency, and one hand must stay on the wheel. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec07-F39 | anchor: A11
Handheld phone fines are $200 to $400 for a first offense, $400 to $600 for a second within 10 years, and $600 to $800 for a third or later offense, which also brings three points and possibly a 90-day suspension. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec07-F40 | anchor: A11
A GDL holder may not use a handheld or hands-free phone, or any other handheld electronic device, while driving. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec07-F41 | anchor: A12
Throwing trash from a moving or parked vehicle is illegal, throwing dangerous objects onto a roadway can bring fines of up to $1,000, and littering from a moving vehicle can cost the driver the license. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0089]

Misconceptions: a yellow light does not mean speed up, it means stop unless you are too close; hands-free phones are legal for most drivers but not for GDL holders; an oncoming car's high beams are answered by looking right, never by flashing back; on a divided highway beyond a median you still slow down for a school bus, you do not ignore it.
Mnemonics: fifteen feet from the rails, twenty-five feet from the bus, ten feet from the hydrant, fifty feet from the stop sign and the tracks; stay three hundred feet behind a running emergency vehicle; headlights from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise.
Glossary: stale green means a signal that has been green for a while and may change soon; Move Over law means the duty to change lanes away from, or slow for, stopped emergency and disabled vehicles; primary offense means a violation police can stop you for on its own; dual-lane highway means a road divided by a safety island or raised median; frozen dessert truck means an ice cream truck using a stop arm and flashing red lights.
Dynamic facts: phone, Move Over and littering fines and points can change; confirm current amounts on the MVC website.
